heading: Control flow
body:
Loops, conditionals and switches are elements, so you can see the structure in the markup. A conditional is always `<logic>`: `<logic :if>`, then `<logic :else-if>`, then `<logic else>`. A loop is always `<loop :for="item of items">`. `<switch>` and `<case>` choose one part by a value. There is no `<if>`, `<else>` or `<for>` element: the build stops with `TY1367` and names the form to use. `ty migrate check` lists these old elements, and `ty migrate fix --write` rewrites them, so `<for :each="item in items">` becomes `<loop :for="item of items">`.

A loop binding (the name of the current item) exists only inside the loop. In `<loop :for="topic of documentation.topics()">`, the binding `topic` has the name of a service. Inside the loop, `topic` reads the item. It does not load `TopicService`.
